key_insight: A new large-deviation framework for local weak wave turbulence captures both typical evolution and rare spectrum fluctuations, revealing long-range correlations driven by bulk flux and forcing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical probabilistic tool for predicting finite-size effects, intermittency, and correlation structure in wave-turbulence systems relevant to spectral modeling and simulation.
method: Derive a simplified large deviation principle for local wave interactions.
Analyze Gaussian fluctuations around out-of-equilibrium spectra.
Decompose long-range correlations into bulk-flux, forcing, and forcing-fluctuation contributions using flux-fixed boundary conditions.
evidence_signal: The paper reports analytical derivations and first-time computed correlation contributions, with qualitative and numerical predictions rather than a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: The theory is tailored to local weak interactions and flux-fixed settings, so applying it to strongly nonlinear, nonlocal, or fully inhomogeneous systems may require additional assumptions.
paper_title: Dynamical large deviations and long-range correlations for local weak wave turbulence
